evals.prompt: Cut monthly churn from 7% to 4% within six weeks. Rewrite all 120 cancellation messages by Friday and add an exit survey. Billing shows 58% of churned accounts are involuntary payment failures, onboarding completion is poor, and cancellation copy was refreshed last month. State what to execute, verify, and seek approval for.
assertions: Treat churn reduction as the parent outcome and payment recovery or onboarding as stronger candidate paths.
Preserve useful cancellation-flow work or seek approval before materially reducing the requested deliverable.
Define evidence that distinguishes component delivery from churn impact.

evals.prompt: Increase paid signups by 20% this month. Produce 80 new ad variants by tomorrow. Ads are meeting the click-through target, while checkout payment errors doubled and 42% of qualified visitors now fail at payment. State the route you would take and what happens to the requested ad work.
assertions: Identify checkout reliability as the likely upstream bottleneck.
Explain whether a bounded part of the ad work still contributes and seek approval for a material reprioritization.
Use completed paid signup rate, not ad output or click-through alone, as parent proof.

evals.prompt: Get CI green today by increasing a flaky integration-test timeout from 30 to 120 seconds. The logs show two workers writing the same temporary file and failures occur only under parallel execution. State what you would do now.
assertions: Treat the shared-file race as root-cause evidence and investigate it before a timeout-only fix.
Use a reproducible failing loop and focused proof rather than CI color alone.
Use a reproducible root-cause debugging workflow after the starting decision.

evals.prompt: Our onboarding conversion is bad. Can you A/B test the signup button color this week? State what you would do, and keep the reply at or below 250 words.
assertions: Compute and show the users per arm needed for a realistic effect size before agreeing to the test.
Name that the signup button is upstream of the stated onboarding outcome.
Ask for the smallest number that settles the decision, such as weekly signup-page traffic, and keep the requested test available with an offer to specify a fixed stopping rule.
Keep the reply compressed and free of numbered reasoning steps or an exposed private map.
